reviews.text: This disaster film is contrived and nonsensical with very few redeeming features.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Greenland may not add anything fresh or new to the very over-done genre of disaster movies, yet it provides two hours of fun and entertaining escapism. Gerard Butler is better than he's been in a while.
reviews.author: Rebecca Johnson

reviews.text: In the end, Greenland is predictably underwhelming, packing only a couple of genuinely exciting sequences, and a decent cast.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: Butler’s most affecting performance in years... Greenland presents the end of the world as we know it in a mighty fine and entertaining way.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: A surprisingly grounded disaster movie featuring Gerard Butler’s best performance in years. The thought-provoking premise and emotional focus elevate this above other movies in this popular subgenre.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: A remarkable combination of downright dullness and eye-rolling coincidences.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: It’s one of Butler’s best films in years; one that takes the familiar end-of-the-world idea and uses it to explore human nature in a surprisingly thoughtful way.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: For most of its runtime, "Greenland" surprises at just about every opportunity. It continually takes every decision that a mindless disaster movie might make and does the complete opposite.
reviews.author: Cody Dericks

reviews.text: It does a good job of masquerading as something deeper than your average disaster fare.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Believable characters keep the story grounded (this is head-and-shoulders above Gerard Butler's ordinary, two-dimensional fare).
reviews.author: Alex Behan

reviews.text: If this isn't exactly how the end of the world will happen, the way [Greenland's] characters learn about the film's cataclysm at least feels eerily believable.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: The movie wants to be on the same scale as War of the Worlds, World War Z or Roland Emmerich's movies, but at a fraction of the budget.
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: By focusing on the stories and lives of people on the ground in favour of a more crash, bang, wallop approach, Greenland offers genuine thrills.
reviews.author: Leonie Cooper

reviews.text: But with a seemingly never-ending pandemic making a non-bunkered lifestyle difficult, if not impossible, until sometime next year, a pre- and post-apocalyptic thriller feels reassuring.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: Greenland [is] no under-the-radar masterpiece waiting to be discovered. Still, there's plenty of space to appreciate a low-budget B movie exceeding expectations.
reviews.author: Daniel Gorman

reviews.text: There are enough quietly compelling moments and plenty of fine performances to justify Greenland as passable entertainment.
reviews.author: Jeff Ames

reviews.text: Waugh's film feels like too much, especially in the final act, when the personal is replaced by the plodding.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: At first, I thought someone had played a practical joke on me.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: The scenes of rioting resemble the news footage that accompanied the reign of President Trump. It was probably unintentional, but the similarities are startling, with the film evoking Americans at war with each other, a theme that is uncomfortably timely.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Sure, there are plenty of explosions and breathtakingly horrifying sequences involving cities being annihilated by fragments of the comet, but the panic-fueled tension at the center of Greenland comes from the real human stakes driving its narrative.
reviews.author: Heather Wixson

reviews.text: If you can ignore the at-times-laughable script this is a skilled, very dark and surprisingly effect disaster movie. (Blu-ray Review).
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Unhappy with the results of GeoStorm (2017), Gerard Butler comes marching again with a brand new by-the-numbers apocalyptic venture. Light in special effects and heavy on drama, just move along folks please...
reviews.author: Alejandro Turdó

reviews.text: Director Ric Roman Waugh has an economic approach to filmmaking which promises a significantly richer experience than the average disaster movie.
reviews.author: Jennie Kermode

reviews.text: It's a silly script, but it's most definitely not stupid. Respect.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: A bona fide disaster flick in the spirit of the modern disaster flick that was re-pioneered by Roland Emmerich.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: The emphasis on people rather than the event makes this one of the best efforts in this very popular genre.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: Butler's a believably imperfect dad and husband who navigates the entertainingly improbably events of the movie with tongue firmly in cheek
reviews.author: Jo Berry

reviews.text: Ric Roman Waugh's Greenland emerges as 2021's first major surprise: yet another large-scale disaster movie, it leaps head-and-shoulders above its genre to become the strongest film of its type since Michael Bay's Armageddon back in 1998.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: What comes out the other end is a paint-by-numbers disaster film with strong enough performances and action to do the job it set out to, but nothing more and nothing less.
reviews.author: Lindsay Traves

reviews.text: The film's strength lies in its intimate approach - we stay close to the family as they travel through a disintegrating landscape of givers and takers - and it is the human focus, rather than the special effects, that ultimately keeps you gripped.
reviews.author: Stephen Applebaum

reviews.text: A typical disaster movie that manages to stand out by writing a more grounded story. Less about the spectacle and more about characters.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Muir

reviews.text: Thrills - not worthwhile characters - are the priority.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: It gives you the same feel as those classic popcorn movies, but it's Butler and Baccarin's performances that give it so much heart, taking the film to a refreshing new level.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: GREENLAND is a throwback that goes through the motions to become a fun film to watch if you want to see the world burn.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: This is a powerful Butler movie which is about more than running, jumping, shouting and shooting.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: ...an effective pulpy, straight-up slice of Armageddon-anxiety circa 2021...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: ...an uneven yet, ultimately, completely rewarding (and above-average) disaster flick.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: The result is a first-rate B-picture, and a timely reminder of the delights of well-crafted popcorn thrills.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: The new movie Greenland will make you sick. And I cannot recommend it highly enough.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Butler's best star vehicle in years, what could have been a bombastic bunch of boulders is, instead, a refreshingly clear-eyed and compelling affair. One of the best disaster movies in years.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt (UK)

reviews.text: Its script might be a broken mess, but the phenomenal performances are what saves Greenland from being a total disaster.
reviews.author: Andrew Murray

reviews.text: It's as if the film knows what we know, or what we've learnt in lockdown. That even in the face of chaos and disaster on a worldwide scale, it's the personal stuff that counts.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Sets the disaster movie bar at a much higher level, and it succeeds. This is a really well done, enjoyable popcorn movie.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: If you love disaster movies because they're a guilty pleasure, this one might offer some challenges. Greenland is actually unsettling, if you care to read its darker meanings.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: It's pitched a little too shrilly, with dramatic moments that don't quite land.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: While [director Ric Roman] Waugh couldn't quite rescue Butler's last film, Angel Has Fallen, from the violent ugliness of its franchise, he at least injected it with a little self-awareness.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: All in all, this is absolutely worth watching despite, at first glance, it purely fulfilling all the stereotypes of a disaster film.
reviews.author: Jenny Desborough

reviews.text: This is a perfectly suitable action film, but Greenland's true drawcard is its dramatic temperament, grounded by a genuine sense of fear and a surprisingly tender turn from [Gerard] Butler
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Knowing the carnage still to come, it was refreshing to meet the Garrity family as a group of regular people that will simply have to try and survive.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: With a surprisingly emotional core and fantastic lead performance from Morena Baccarin, Greenland isn't necessarily the Gerard Butler film you'd expect
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: Gerard Butler finally faces an adversary he can't punch.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: A disaster movie mostly made from spare parts, Greenland is an unoriginal and hardly brain-taxing race against time. But that doesn't negate its entertainment value or heart-pounding pace.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: Far bleaker and more downbeat than you would expect. The film manages something truly unique by showing that you don't need astronomical budgets to make a decent disaster movie.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: [Waugh] brings some humanity and palpable jeopardy to a story we've seen myriad times before. This is up there with Butler's best work too, especially in the film's nailbiting early stages.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Thanks to empathetic characterisation and a plot that moves effectively and rivetingly, Greenland really works.
reviews.author: Deirdre Molumby

reviews.text: It still has all the apocalyptic elements you'd expect from a big Hollywood action film. They're just not always front and centre.
reviews.author: Rob Aldam

reviews.text: Better than most other large scale disaster films out there, Greenland shifts its focus away from an abundance of speaker rumbling explosions and near misses
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Greenland is one of the better disaster movies of the century and, for my part, the best one since 2004's The Day After Tomorrow.
reviews.author: Rhys Bowen Jones

reviews.text: While not a peak of the genre, Greenland is overall an honest example of it. [Full review in French]

reviews.text: Ladies and gents, there's nothing like a good popcorn thriller right in the middle of Oscar season. It's like finding a hidden chocolate bar during an expensive dinner party.

reviews.text: It's grim, ugly, violent and frustrating, mirroring how it makes me feel.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: The last smart disaster movie I can think of...
reviews.author: Martin Thomas

reviews.text: We haven't had something like this for a while...a smart disaster movie.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Butler, for his part, does the best he can with a role that doesn't feel too natural to him. [Full review in Spanish]

reviews.text: Greenland is a decent enough addition to the disaster catalog structurally, but it's a comfortable distance from the halls of greatness due to a lack of fun.

reviews.text: A compelling survival thriller that elevates the disaster movie sub-genre. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: It is a disaster pic, but it often feels more like a family drama, and that is to the credit of Greenland.
reviews.author: Dustin Rowles

reviews.text: The latest Gerard Butler vehicle doesn't add much to the global disaster genre. Hell, it doesn't add much to this year.
reviews.author: Chance Solem-Pfeifer

reviews.text: With an eye for detail, but ultimately a bit too formulaic... this apocalyptic setting offers decent entertainment. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: A same-old tale of apocalypse knows we've seen this all before, and so centers human drama over disaster porn. It has nothing new to say, but at least it says it well, with notes of horrific grace.

reviews.text: "Deep Impact" it's not. What unspools is a far shallower collision between the heavens and Earth, where all life beyond the Garritys is rife for enhancing a rapidly climbing body count.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Coming after the hot mess that was Geostorm, one might be wary about another end of the world Gerard Butler film. Greenland, however, surprises by being both a fun ride and well executed.
reviews.author: Bill Watters

reviews.text: As meteors of unprecedented size and scope, not to mention one massive earthquake, turn the world into a smoldering ruin, causing millions to lose their lives and their loved ones, we have to ask ourselves, do I really need to see this... in a pandemic?
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: Greenland soars above the usual end-of-the-world disaster mayhem because it focuses on a family's fight to survive. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: You may find yourself rooting for the only sympathetic character in the movie: the comet.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: Greenland isn't a great film, but it is far better than I expected it to be...It doesn't all make sense, but it doesn't have to - just go along for the ride and you'll have a good time.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: Typical genre fare at worst, and truly ingenious genre fare at best.

reviews.text: The enticing film has a hokey story but gives us the required thrills a thriller needs.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: A disaster-thriller that champions humanity over calamity, 'Greenland' is a welcome reminder of the oft-out-of-nowhere thrills that await us at the cineplexes.

reviews.text: Just an average "end of the world" movie. Butler and Baccarin couldn't have any less chemistry if they tried.

reviews.text: Greenland isn't going to change anybody's life, but it elevates disaster-movie tropes just enough to make it worth a watch.

reviews.text: You know, if comets were made of farts, this might have been a fun film.

reviews.text: I'm shocked at how good this movie is, because on paper it looked totally stupid... Surprisingly gripping and well-done.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Gerard Butler's latest effort reveals a dramatic depth beneath the action man veneer. Brooding, bold and effortlessly engaging, Greenland breaks the mould.

reviews.text: It's a surprisingly entertaining popcorn ride.

reviews.text: [Director Ric Roman Waugh and star Gerard Butler's] latest outing is a bit more enthusiastic though no less derivative than countless disaster epics which focus on extinction level events waged by the heavens.

reviews.text: But no matter how silly it all gets the reality of the situation for the family is rarely inauthentic, making the ridiculous stupidity even easier to digest.

reviews.text: Unexpectedly more dramatic than action packed with strong, subtle performances from its leads Greenland doesn't offer enough new to really sustain its concept but there are worse ways to spend a few hours.

reviews.text: Delivering the apocalypse on a budget, the disaster film Greenland dramatises the end of the world with no-nonsense efficiency.

reviews.text: The themes of privilege and inequality, ideas the movie mostly commits to despite some shortcomings, is what makes Greenland much more interesting than it has any right to be.

reviews.text: Your reaction may vary, but I believe Greenland is genuinely trying to do something different within the disaster film genre, and I appreciate and even admire the effort.

reviews.text: Greenland is an apocalyptic movie that isn't going to change the world, but it largely succeeds in being suspenseful, escapist entertainment.

reviews.text: Nothing that happens in Greenland is all that surprising, including the poor and shrewdly opportunist ways people react under pressure.

reviews.text: A decent pending Apocalypse thriller with good performances and some nice emotional touches. (Full Content Review for Parents - Violence, Profanity, etc. - also Available)

synopsis: John Garrity, his estranged wife and their young son embark on a perilous journey to find sanctuary as a planet-killing comet hurtles toward Earth. Amid terrifying accounts of cities getting leveled, the Garrity's experience the best and worst in humanity. As the countdown to the global apocalypse approaches zero, their incredible trek culminates in a desperate and last-minute flight to a possible safe haven.
